## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
## load libraries ##
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(dplyr)

## load data ##
glimpse(penguins)

## clean data ##
palmer_clean <- penguins |>
  select(species,sex,year,bill_length_mm,body_mass_g)
glimpse(palmer_clean)



## ggplot ##
#|out-width:70% # changes the size of your figure
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()

```

```{r}
## ggplot ##
#|fig-width: 3 # inputs exact size (inches) of figure
#|fig-width: 5
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()


```

```{r}

## ggplot ##
#| fig-align:"center" # puts figure in the center of the rendering
ggplot(data=palmer_clean,mapping = aes(x=species, y=bill_length_mm))+
  geom_boxplot()

```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
